scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4659: Hi IT!! The campus network keeps going SLOW in bursts.
People here say it might be router0, but I don't know if that is right.
Something around the main router box must be overloaded. Could someone look at
router0 and make the network stop crawling!!! Thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 has ip_forward enabled, its interfaces
  are up, and traffic transiting router0 between segments arrives with 0% loss; there
  is no drop-inducing ACL or forwarding fault. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of packet loss on router0 that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router0 dropping/forwarding
traffic incorrectly -- is NOT reproducible: a ping across router0 (between two
segments it connects) completes with 0% loss, router0 has ip_forward enabled, its
interfaces are up, ripd is running, and there is no drop-inducing ACL.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router0 is forwarding correctly and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a path transiting
router0, finds 0% loss, checks router0's ip_forward, interfaces, and any filters, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" router0 dropping packets -- blaming an ACL,
forwarding, or load to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
We investigated the core (router0) and the inter-router links for overload, queuing, or routing instability and found no evidence of a fault. On router0, CPU and memory are idle (load avg ~0.1), IP forwarding is enabled, and FRR/RIP routes are stable. All router0 interfaces (eth0/eth1/eth2) and the adjacent switches show zero queuing drops and negligible traffic in tc/ethtool stats, ruling out bufferbloat or microburst-induced loss. End-to-end tests reflect normal latency (pings 2–4 ms across campus) and steady TCP throughput around 40–50 Mbit/s from multiple subnets, with only small, transient dips that are consistent with normal TCP window dynamics rather than congestion. RIP routing tables on router0/1/2 are consistent, with expected metrics and no signs of route churn; the WAN links (10.10.0.0/8 and 20.20.0.0/8) are up and not dropping packets.

Localization: No abnormal CPU, queue, or error counters were observed on router0 (or the R0–R1 link), and adjacent distribution routers (router1, router2) are similarly healthy.

Root cause: Not reproducible on the network core; router0 is not overloaded and is not the source of the reported “bursty slowness.”

Corrective fix: No change required on router0. To capture intermittent issues, deploy interface/queue telemetry (e.g., periodic tc -s qdisc and ip -s link polling) and consider enabling flow monitoring on edge segments where user contention is likely. If slowness recurs, correlate timestamps with edge utilization to identify the true hotspot.
